The item supplies neither a quarterly Azure inference series through September 2025 nor a January–September 2025 subtotal, so it cannot settle whether spending rose consistently or reached at least twice the full-year 2024 total [e1].
limitations: Neither the claimed 2024 baseline nor the January–September 2025 subtotal is independently authenticated on a comparable basis.

The lower 2024 estimate remains unreconciled with the claimed realized expenses.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI's inference costs rose consistently, from $3.76 billion in 2024 to more than double that through September 2025.

statement.excerpt: OpenAI’s inference costs have risen consistently over the last 18 months, too. For example, OpenAI spent $3.76 billion on inference in CY2024, meaning that OpenAI has already doubled its inference costs in CY2025 through September.
statement.document_title: Exclusive: Here's How Much OpenAI Spends On Inference and Its Revenue Share With Microsoft

from_speaker: already doubled its inference costs in CY2025 through September
our_interpretation: Costs means aggregate spending, not the price per token or per unit of capability.
Azure scope carries over from the surrounding discussion.
Use calendar quarters to test the trend. Read the last 18 months as the six completed quarters ending September 2025, with Q1 2024 as the preceding comparison quarter.
The target period also includes all of 2024 because that full-year amount is the explicit comparison baseline.
Doubled means the January–September 2025 subtotal reached at least twice the full-year 2024 total, without annualizing either amount.
Use estimate for the journalistic financial figures. Small rounding differences alone do not disprove the stated 2024 baseline.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable records establish approximately $3.76 billion in 2024 Azure inference expenses, increases across the quarterly comparison sequence, and January–September 2025 expenses of at least twice the 2024 total.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records establish a materially different 2024 baseline, fail the doubling test, or show a sustained reversal inconsistent with the claimed consistent rise. An isolated quarterly decline bears on the stricter quarterly reading and must be identified separately.
